agent_notes: Sources renumbered to Psalms 63:11. Yagiruhu is a plural verb with a singular object: the commentators split between a singular victim (Radak, Meiri: Saul) and a collective. The literal layer keeps 'him' and 'they'. Shu'alim is the ordinary word for foxes, though jackals are possible in carrion contexts; I keep 'foxes' as all five versions do.

agent_notes: Sources renumbered to Psalms 63:12. The antecedent of 'by him' (bo) is disputed: God (Rashi, Radak, Metzudat David), or the king (Meiri, Malbim's second option). Ibn Ezra reports that some say the oath was Saul's. The literal layer keeps 'by him'; the dramatic layer chooses God, which the next clause (liars silenced) supports as an oath-keeping contrast. Radak attributes the lying oath to Saul's oath to the LORD not to kill David; this is the commentator's reading, not the text's.

agent_notes: STEPBible glosses אֵלִי as 'God my' and אֲשַׁחֲרֶךָּ as 'I am seeking earnestly'. I kept 'my God' and 'I seek you' and noted the dawn-root pun (shachar) in the notes. The KJV, ASV and Webster say 'early', and YLT says 'earnestly'; the pun is possible but not certain, so I flagged it as such.

The line 've'ayef beli-mayim' is not a clause but a noun phrase: 'a land of dryness and weariness, without water'. Radak, Ibn Ezra and Meiri read 'ayef' as an adjective on 'eretz' (feminine noun used as masculine), while Metzudat Zion glosses it as 'dry'. I kept 'weary' in the literal layer and 'parched' in the dramatic one.

agent_notes: The Hebrew 'ken baqodesh chazitikha' puts the sanctuary vision first, and the KJV reverses the order ('to see thy power... so as I have seen thee'). Rashi reads 'ken' as 'ka'asher' (as/just as). I follow the Hebrew order and take 'ken' as 'so, thus'. Whether the sanctuary vision is memory (past perfect) or a present inner vision (Malbim) is open.

Sources for the chesed note are now commentaries in the packet (Metzudat David, Malbim on Psalms 63:4); the BDB/HALOT citations are dropped. The gloss 'covenant loyalty' for chesed is my own reading, flagged as such in the note.

agent_notes: The earlier sentence that two of the psalm's body words recur was wrong. Verse 2 has soul and flesh, verse 6 has soul and mouth, so only 'soul' (nefesh) recurs, and the commentary now says only that. The five English versions split on 'marrow and fatness' (KJV, ASV, Webster), 'milk and fatness' (YLT, a misreading of chelev as chalav) and 'good food' (BBE); I keep 'fat and fatness'. For 'my mouth' (pi), the literal layer keeps the Hebrew third-person verb 'it will praise' without a bracketed object, since the Hebrew has none.
